subject: Pre-sales traffic audit & fleet planning for Dedicated (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ronald Wu <ronald.wu@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample traffic

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for taking time today. As discussed on the call, we're trying to get a realistic GPU fleet estimate for a Dedicated deployment. I've attached a small sample CSV that contains 7 days of anonymized request logs (timestamp, model, prompt_len_tokens, completion_len_tokens, user_id_hash). High level: average QPS today is ~8 with 50 concurrent users at peak business hours, but we expect a product launch spike up to 250 QPS for short bursts.

Our SLO target is 95th percentile tail latency <= 350ms for standard chat flows, and we use an in-house reranker for retrieval-augmented prompts. We plan to serve a mix of Llama-2-70B and a smaller 13B for low-cost routes.

Can your pre-sales team review and recommend:
- a conservative GPU fleet sizing for steady-state and burst capacity,
- suggestions on model pinning and fallback policy,
- whether KV/prefix caching will materially change expected concurrency, and
- any immediate data you need from us (e.g., token distribution percentiles, warm-up patterns).

Attachment: acme_sample_traffic.csv (CSV, 46KB)

Appreciate the help — happy to set up a follow-up workshop if useful.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Health

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample traffic

Hi Elena — thanks for the CSV and the clear ask. I've looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Dev (solutions SE) so we can give a complete fleet and cost picture. A few quick clarifying questions before we run the sizing runbook: 

1) Can you share the token distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p95) for prompt and completion if available? The CSV helps but token buckets matter for batching and memory.
2) For the "spike to 250 QPS" — is that sustained for >10 minutes or bursts of ~1–3 minutes tied to marketing events?
3) Do you expect many long contexts (e.g., >2k tokens) for the Llama-2-70B flows?
4) Any hard constraints on cost or preferred GPU SKUs (A100, H100, etc.)?

Action: we'll review the CSV and run a short probe (simulated) traffic model against our throughput curves. We'll also attach the Redwood sizing template to collect the rest of the workload metadata.

Next step: can we schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop on Thursday or Friday this week to finalize assumptions?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample traffic

Raf & Dev — quick internal notes before we reply to Acme: 

- Given the stated p95 SLO (350ms) and mix of 70B + 13B, plan should assume:
  * steady-state reserve: enough capacity for 2x current avg QPS (so ~16 QPS baseline) to cover growth and retries,
  * burst headroom: ability to absorb 250 QPS for short spikes via burst pool (elastic) and model fallback to 13B or quantized 70B variant.
- Check if Acme will accept graceful degradation: route lower-priority inference to 13B during spikes to hit latency SLOs.
- Cache: prefix/KV caching will significantly reduce token compute if users are repeat querying similar contexts; need percent of repeat sessions.
- Warm pools: pre-warmed model instances for L2-70B are likely required to meet p95 target; cold starts will blow the SLO.

Dev — can you run a quick throughput estimate for: 70B FP16 vs 70B Q4 (quantized), both at sequence lengths 512 and 2048 with the CSV baseline? Also prepare a short slide with expected GPU counts for: steady-state, 3x growth, and 250 QPS burst with fallback rules.

I'll propose two slots for the customer once we confirm their answers.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ronald Wu <ronald.wu@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample traffic

Hi Rafael/Marissa/Dev — answers below inline: 

1) Token percentiles (prompt / completion): p50: 128/64, p90: 420/180, p95: 820/420. We have a long-tail for some debug-heavy sessions but the majority stay under 600 tokens total.
2) Spike profile: marketing-driven spikes are typically short — 2–8 minutes — but can repeat several times in an hour during big campaigns. We expect 2–3 large spikes in the first 30 days after launch.
3) Long contexts: ~7% of requests use >2k tokens (medical record summaries), but those are lower QPS flows and can be routed to dedicated RAG workers.
4) Preferred GPU SKUs: not mandated, but cost sensitivity favors options using quantized variants on more cost-efficient hardware.

We also attached an internal latency extract (p50/p90/p95) from our current host — p95 is currently ~680ms in our test environment. Hoping Redwood's Dedicated config can bring that down.

Happy to join a sizing workshop Friday afternoon (09/17) at 1:00pm PT if that works.

Attachment: p95_latency_report.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

Thanks,
Elena

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales traffic audit & fleet planning for Dedicated (Acme Health)

Elena — great, thank you for the token percentiles and the latency extract. Plan of record and next steps: 

1) We'll run two simulated sizing passes (today):
   a) Conservative plan: steady-state for 2x avg QPS + reserved burst pool for 250 QPS (handles 5-minute sustained spikes). This will primarily use a mix of H100-backed instances for L2-70B quantized variants and A100/80GB for unquantized 13B where latency-sensitive.
   b) Cost-optimized plan: more aggressive fallback to 13B and quantized 70B on cheaper GPUs, with autoscaling windows tuned to absorb the 2–8 minute spikes without overprovisioning.

2) Dev will share throughput tables (tokens/sec per GPU for each model/quantization/seq-length) and proposed GPU-counts for each plan in a short deck.
3) We'll include explicit model-pinning/fallback routing rules and an ops runbook for warm pools + cold-start mitigation.
4) Sizing workshop: Friday 2027-09-17 13:00 PT — invited. We'll send a calendar invite with a prep doc and expected decisions.

Please confirm the workshop slot and any additional stakeholders to include.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
